candidateAudit.title: „Die Gastronomie muss teurer werden.“⁠ ⁠ Steigende Personal-, Lebensmittel- und Betriebskosten treffen die Gastronomie massiv. Gleichzeitig wollen Gäste verständlicherweise nicht p
candidateAudit.text: „Die Gastronomie muss teurer werden.“⁠ ⁠ Steigende Personal-, Lebensmittel- und Betriebskosten treffen die Gastronomie massiv. Gleichzeitig wollen Gäste verständlicherweise nicht plötzlich 40 Euro für ein Schnitzel bezahlen. Wie kann dieser Spagat funktionieren?⁠ ⁠ In der neuen Podcast-Folge von NEXT GEN spricht Ferdinand Querfeld mit Desirée Fellner über die Zukunft der Gastronomie, die Herausforderungen eines traditionsreichen Familienunternehmens und darüber, wie sich die Wiener Kaffeehauskultur verändern muss, um bestehen zu können.⁠ ⁠ Querfeld erklärt, warum höhere Preise teilweise unvermeidbar sind – und warum es trotzdem entscheidend ist, ein Angebot zu schaffen, das fair für den Betrieb und für den Gast bleibt. Denn am Ende soll niemand das Lokal verlassen und das Gefühl haben, „übers Ohr gehauen“ worden zu sein.⁠ ⁠ 🎧 Die ganze Folge jetzt überall hören, wo es Podcasts gibt! #linkinbio⁠ ⁠ #cafelandtmann #dasbootshaus #familiequerfeld #nextgen #podcast

candidateAudit.title: GEHEIMTIPP IN WIEN 🌳 📍Bank Austria Park, Mühlschüttelgasse bis Drygalskiweg, 1210 Wien An der Oberen Alten Donau gibt es einen Kunsterlebnis-Park mit Kunstwerken von 14 nationale
candidateAudit.text: GEHEIMTIPP IN WIEN 🌳 📍Bank Austria Park, Mühlschüttelgasse bis Drygalskiweg, 1210 Wien An der Oberen Alten Donau gibt es einen Kunsterlebnis-Park mit Kunstwerken von 14 nationalen und internationalen KünstlerInnen.🎨 Neben den Skulpturen gefällt mir besonders, wie schön der Park gestaltet ist: mit Blumen, Bäumen und vielen Sitzgelegenheiten, zum Teil auch mit Tischen oder Liegen.🌺 Der Eintritt ist frei und der Park jederzeit zugänglich. Wenn du die QR-Codes bei den Kunstwerken scannst, bekommst du außerdem Infos über die Künstlerlnnen und ihre Werke. Beim Vorbeispazieren habe ich direkt daneben außerdem einen richtig schönen, großen Spielplatz und einige Outdoor-Sportgeräte entdeckt.🛝 🚌 ANFAHRT: Am besten mit dem Bus 33A bis Mühlschüttel oder mit der Straßenbahn 25 oder 26 bis Fultonstraße (+ ca. 7 Minuten zu Fuß). Ich finde, gerade die Lage macht den Park besonders, direkt an der Alten Donau und nur ein paar Schritte von den kleinen Stegen am Wasser entfernt.🌊☀️ Viel Spaß beim Entdecken!🥰 #wientipps #gratiswien

candidateAudit.text: Wien hat so viele schöne Buschenschanken und einige davon mag ich besonders gerne. Dazu gehört definitiv auch die Buschenschank Esse. 🍇 Von außen spaziert man fast daran vorbei, aber sobald man im Gastgarten sitzt, fühlt es sich an wie ein kleines verstecktes Paradies mitten im Grünen: gemütlich, liebevoll gestaltet und einfach ein Wohlfühlort. Zu essen gibt es kalte und warme Speisen, von Aufstrichen und Kürbiscremesuppe bis hin zu Gulasch, Schweinsbraten, Eierschwammerl oder sogar Burger und natürlich verschiedene Weine, zum Teil aus eigenem Anbau. 🍷 📍 Buschenschank Esse, Wildgrubgasse 44, 1190 Vienna ⏰ ÖFFNUNGSZEITEN: nur an ausgewählten Wochenenden/Feiertagen und bei Schönwetter (kein Innenbereich) ‼️ Die nächsten Termine: 10./11. candidateAudit.title: Was zunächst ungewöhnlich klingt, kann einen wichtigen Beitrag zur Gesundheit leisten: #SocialPrescribing. Denn Gesundheit bedeutet mehr als die Behandlung von Krankheiten. Auch Ei
candidateAudit.text: Was zunächst ungewöhnlich klingt, kann einen wichtigen Beitrag zur Gesundheit leisten: #SocialPrescribing. Denn Gesundheit bedeutet mehr als die Behandlung von Krankheiten. Auch Einsamkeit und soziale Isolation können das Wohlbefinden belasten – besonders für Menschen in Armut oder ohne Zuhause. Stigmatisierung, Ausgrenzung und der Verlust des sozialen Umfelds erschweren oft die soziale Teilhabe. #SocialPrescribing unterstützt Menschen dabei, passende Angebote und neue soziale Kontakte zu finden – etwa in Sportgruppen, Koch- oder Yogakursen oder bei gemeinsamen Museumsbesuchen. Begegnung und Gemeinschaft können helfen, wieder Anschluss zu finden. Mahdi M. hat das selbst erlebt: Nach einer schweren psychischen Krise, Sucht und Obdachlosigkeit wurde Yoga für ihn zu einer wichtigen Ressource. Heute begleitet er als Peer andere Menschen in der Wohnungslosenhilfe. Gerade im #YellowSeptember gilt: 💛 Einsamkeit ist mehr als Alleinsein. 💛 Soziale Verbindung ist wichtig für unsere Gesundheit. 💛 Manchmal braucht es Unterstützung, um wieder Anschluss zu finden. Was könnte dir guttun, wenn du dich einsam fühlst? ℹ️ Der #YellowSeptember verbindet den Tag der Suizidprävention am 10. September mit dem Tag der psychischen Gesundheit am 10. Oktober. Er macht psychosoziale Gesundheit sichtbar und setzt ein starkes Zeichen gegen Einsamkeit. #YellowAwarenessMonth #Einsamkeit #SocialPrescribing #Gesundheit #sozialeTeilhabe #neunerhaus #Wohnungslosigkeit #Obdachlosigkeit #Wien

candidateAudit.text: Seit ich Mama bin, ist Stillen für mich zu etwas so Selbstverständlichem geworden. Wenn meine Tochter Hunger hat, stille ich sie. Und da is es mir egal ob wir gerade zu Hause, unterwegs oder in einem Café sitzen. Anfangs habe ich mir noch viel mehr Gedanken darüber gemacht, ob jemand schaut oder sich vielleicht gestört fühlen könnte. Mittlerweile denke ich mir: Mein Baby isst gerade. Mehr passiert hier eigentlich nicht. 🤍 Ich versuche dabei natürlich nicht, mich demonstrativ zu zeigen, aber genauso wenig möchte ich mich verstecken oder jedes Mal einen anderen Ort suchen müssen. Ich möchte meinen Kaffee trinken, mich mit Freunden unterhalten und gleichzeitig mein Baby stillen können. ☕️🤱🏼 Wie geht ihr damit um? Stillt ihr überall ganz selbstverständlich oder fühlt ihr euch in der Öffentlichkeit manchmal noch unwohl? #ichstillewoichwill #stilleninderöffentlichkeit #mommylife #stillen #trending

candidateAudit.title: Artificial intelligence is often framed as a quest to replicate the human brain, promising frictionless cognition and a future of seamless automation. But what if this pervasive na
candidateAudit.text: Artificial intelligence is often framed as a quest to replicate the human brain, promising frictionless cognition and a future of seamless automation. But what if this pervasive narrative obscures a deeper, more ‘errant’ truth? Media theorist and author Clemens Apprich in conversation with philosopher Jan Völker. Moderated by Amanda Holmes, Department of Philosophy, University of Applied Arts Vienna Welcome: Ulrike Kuch, Rector of the University of Applied Arts Vienna A cooperation of the department of Media Theory and the department of Philosophy. ‘Errant Intelligence’ challenges the prevailing biological and individualistic interpretations of machine learning, arguing instead for a radical understanding of machine intelligence. The book embraces the deviations, inconsistencies, and ‘errant behaviour’ as fundamental to the discovery of new knowledge, moving beyond the illusion of mere optimisation. Drawing on media theory, cybernetics, and a unique psychoanalytic lens, it explores the ‘technological unconscious’ of machine learning. It traces the historical roots of AI, from early automatons and the Turing machine to natural language processing and contemporary machine learning systems. Challenging the idea of an autonomous, self-generating AI, the book exposes the hidden labour, assumed logics, and inherent biases that animate its operation. It re-evaluates computational thinking, insisting on its inherently social, collective, and symbolic character, and revealing how language and logical paradoxes are not obstacles but constitutive forces that shape intelligent machines

Die Zahl der Arbeitslosen sank um 1,1 %, jene der Schulungsteilnehmer_innen um 4,6 %. Insgesamt sind damit 1,9 % weniger Menschen arbeitslos oder in Schulung. AMS-Wien-Chef Winfried Göschl sieht darin eine gute Basis für Optimismus: „Die Lage ist in Wien deutlich besser als die Stimmung.“ Besonders erfreulich: Die Zahl der unter 25-Jährigen, die arbeitslos oder in Schulung sind, ist um 5,4 % gesunken. Und auch für alle, die im Herbst auf Jobsuche sind, gibt es Chancen: Gerade in Tourismus und Gastronomie werden in anderen Bundesländern viele Arbeitskräfte gesucht. candidateAudit.text: In this workshop with Helena Detsch we will explore simple ways to create a fascinating natural color palette from soil and plant-based materials like earths, minerals, vegetables, kitchen supplies and algae pigments. Part of the exhibition ‘03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis’ Duration: 15:30–17:30 Please register for this workshop via link in bio (free entry) Together, we'll first experiment with making self-made oil- or watercolors from 100% natural sources and then explore the many possibilities of sustainable painting, discovering how these self-made colors behave on paper and fabric and what a truly organic painting practice can look like. In her oil paintings, installations and animations, Helena Detsch explores (mis-)relationships between humans and more-than-human life. Her series and immersive spatial installations question Western anthropocentric narratives about nature as a resource and create spaces to reflect on coexistence and complex interconnections between human and other agents. To develop a more sustainable art practice, she crafts natural colors from plant and soil pigments. helena.kettu AIL, Otto Wagner-Postsparkasse / Georg-Coch-Platz 2, 1010 Vienna dieangewandte

candidateAudit.text: About the next exhibition at AIL: Soil is a highly diverse and sensitive cosmos that is facing increasing pressure due to the climate crisis, as a result of more frequent and severe extreme events such as drought. Soil holds histories, stories and belowground storage systems, repositories of information and traces of past worlds, current developments and future scenarios. What is happening beneath our feet? At AIL researchers and artists show their open, collaborative process, which unfolds in a multiperspective inquiry on soil and drought. candidateAudit.title: Coming up next as part of VIENNA DESIGN WEEK 2026 🪢 The exhibition ’Zero and One Chairs’ was created as part of MATCH!, a recurring initiative organised by the department of Appli
candidateAudit.text: Coming up next as part of VIENNA DESIGN WEEK 2026 🪢 The exhibition ’Zero and One Chairs’ was created as part of MATCH!, a recurring initiative organised by the department of Applied Photography and Time-Based Media at the University of Applied Arts Vienna, which explores the synergistic potential of student teams from different degree programs. In collaboration with the department Industrial Design, this year’s focus was on the intersection of photography and the object, with particular attention paid to the relationship with set design, styling, casting and narrative. Seen from the perspective of Applied Photography, the object and thus the chair, is a welcome protagonist. Photography’s multiple applied genres are cited here: documentary, fashion, advertising, architecture and the portrait. When the function in Industrial Design coalesces with the idea of the purpose in Applied Photography, the question of factuality emerges. Be not mistaken: The most literal things are often the most confusing and enigmatic. Between what it is and how it is*, worlds unfold. We put the images to work. VDW Cocktail: 29 Sep, 17:00–18:00 Showcase and drinks followed by a collective walk to the billboards in front of the main entrance of the University Open Saturdays: 26 Sep / 3 Oct, 11:00–18:00 Opening hours: Mon–Fri: 11:00–18:00 AIL, Otto Wagner-Postsparkasse / Georg-Coch-Platz 2, 1010 Vienna The collaborative works are on display at the AIL and on the billboards at the university’s main entrance on Oskar-Kokoschka-Platz. dieangewandte viennadesignweek applied.photography angewandte_id Feat

The artist and researcher duo MUELLER-DIVJAK (Dr. Jeanette Müller and Dr. Paul Divjak), who is working at the AIL with international artists and systems scientists on the FWF/PEEK project SENSING LIVING SYSTEMS. Exploring the Potentials of Multisensory Scenographies for Systems Awareness (Project lead: Mag. Alexandra Graupner; University of Applied Arts), is devoted to creating experiential multisensory spaces – the so called SΫS SPACEs – that help enhancing systems awareness through special sensory cues. Such allowing for coping resiliently with the complex interrelations and interactions that shape our world and all our lives. mueller_divjak dieangewandte

candidateAudit.title: The Unsafe+Sounds festival, held annually in Vienna, returns in September with a kaleidoscopic program, offering a multifaceted glimpse into the contemporary music scene and AIL is
candidateAudit.text: The Unsafe+Sounds festival, held annually in Vienna, returns in September with a kaleidoscopic program, offering a multifaceted glimpse into the contemporary music scene and AIL is delighted to once again host one event in the program. unsafeandsounds AIL, Otto Wagner-Postsparkasse / Georg-Coch-Platz 2, 1010 Vienna (Free entry) Overview: 18:30 Panel Discussion, unsafe+sounds in cooperation with the Weibel Institute for Digital Cultures (University of Applied Arts Vienna) weibel.institute Affective Histories Timotheus Vermeulen and Christian Höller in conversation with Sophie Publig History is never simply given. It is made through the scales and materials by which the past becomes legible: from sweeping narratives and historical events to gestures, sounds, images, technical infrastructures, and seemingly minor traces SOPHIE PUBLIG is a Senior Scientist researching digital ecosystems. Based at the Weibel Institute for Digital Cultures at the University of Applied Arts Vienna, she navigates the intricate networks of online territories. TIMOTHEUS VERMEULEN is Professor of Media, Culture and Society at the University of Oslo and joint director of the Media Aesthetics Research Group. He was a visiting scholar in Art History at Harvard in 2023–24 and will serve as joint Principal Investigator on a project on the politics of tone at the Centre for Advanced Study in Oslo in 2027–28. CHRISTIAN HÖLLER is editor and co-publisher of springerin – Hefte für Gegenwartskunst. Since 2024 he is head of the department Cross Disciplinary Strategies at the University of Applied Arts Vienna. cro

candidateAudit.text: 📉 Immer weniger Lehrstellen, immer mehr Jugendliche auf der Suche: Aktuell sind in Wien 5.440 Lehrstellensuchende beim AMS vorgemerkt, aber nur 496 offene Lehrstellen gemeldet. Das sind wohlgemerkt 37,8 % weniger Lehrstellen als vor einem Jahr. AMS-Wien-Chef Winfried Göschl appelliert an die Unternehmen, selbst auszubilden und damit in die Fachkräfte von morgen zu investieren. Denn: „Unternehmen, die nicht ausbilden, lassen viel Potenzial liegen.“ Für Jugendliche, bei denen es mit der Lehrstelle nicht klappt, gibt’s mit der Überbetrieblichen Lehrausbildung (ÜBA) trotzdem viele Möglichkeiten, einen Lehrabschluss zu machen. 💪 🔗 Alle weiteren Details zu den aktuelles Arbeitsmarktdaten findest du in unserer Presseaussendung. candidateAudit.title: Throughout August and September, the artist duo MUELLER-DIVJAK is residing at AIL for Summer Studio – using the space for artistic research, experimentation, and learning, developi
candidateAudit.text: Throughout August and September, the artist duo MUELLER-DIVJAK is residing at AIL for Summer Studio – using the space for artistic research, experimentation, and learning, developing the project's multisensory scenography – the so-called SΫS SPACE. Aim of the Summer Studio is to prepare the prototype of the scenography, which will be established at the AIL in June 2027 as the centerpiece of the final exhibition of the PEEK project ’SENSING LIVING SYSTEMS — Exploring the Potentials of Multisensory Scenography for Systems Awareness.’ The SΫS SPACE facilitates a physical experience of one's own embededdness within living systems, within complex interrelationships – within a greater whole. It paves the way for relational sensing and thinking – an embodied systems awareness, that can help in coping with complexity, challenges, and uncertainties, and in making good decisions towards sustainable futures. It deliberately reduces the dominance of the sense of sight, placing the emphasis instead on smell, touch, and hearing. Numerous scientists, as well as invited artists, politicians, journalists, children, senior citizens, curators, cultural workers, educators, and teenagers are individually guided through the immersive environment by Jeanette Müller and Paul Divjak and share their responses in photo-based reflections and semi-structured interviews. Their feedback directly informs the prototype. Save the date! 14 and 15 Sep 2026 The SΫS SPACE will open to the public in individual time slots for an exclusive multisensory experience. candidateAudit.title: The exhibition [REVERBERATED]. Following the Movement of Memory is still running till this Friday, July 10! Mon–Fri: 11:00–18:00 Last guided tour: Thur, July 9, 17:00 Memory is not
candidateAudit.text: The exhibition [REVERBERATED]. Following the Movement of Memory is still running till this Friday, July 10! Mon–Fri: 11:00–18:00 Last guided tour: Thur, July 9, 17:00 Memory is not a stable record of the past. Rather than functioning as a static archive, it unfolds as a dynamic process in which traces are continuously reshaped by perception, narration, and material conditions. Across these artistic approaches, [REVERBERATED] invites visitors to consider memory not as something simply preserved, but as something continuously produced through interactions between bodies, technologies, and environments. The exhibition thus explores how the past continues to reverberate within the systems of the present. With contributions by: Agustina Belén Agüero, Lobna Awidat, Phin Anibal, Rimon Alyagon Darr, Ronnie Danaher, Tatiana Del Valle, Hasti Ghasedi, Leah Barbara Mukui Giertz, Hanna Hofmann, Tal Horesh, Mauritius Itzinger, Laura Isselhorst, Dina Karaman, Moritz Klarer, Anna Buchner, Leonard Otterbein, David Ristić, Rajarshi Sarkar, Agnes Schyberg, Aryan Shahabian, Majedeh Shahvelayati, Mehrta Shirzadian, Pauline Simon, Laura Chalabi, People of Soil Photos: Lea Dörl

candidateAudit.text: A new series of postcards is now installed at Café Exchange cafe_exchange The series was extracted from the course ‘Drawing: Here & Now’ by Simon Goritschnig zeichnungunddruckgrafik In collaborative drawing, two people share a single pen – the line becomes a space of negotiation. A play between control and letting go. Who leads – and when? Impulse meets resistance, conviction meets empathy. Not always a conversation, but always an understanding – a dance on paper. These and other experiments are part of the course “Drawing: Here & Now” by Simon Goritschnig, in which students of the department Drawing and Printmaking explore various qualities of drawing beyond observational study. In the project “Reflex,” these experimental setups are set against observational drawing. Students draw in the cashier hall of the former Postsparkasse, intuitively picking up details from architecture and space, as well as situations of coming together: conversations, movements, gazes. In this process, it becomes visible how public and social space is visually probed and explored. The focus lies on reflection — with, through, and within drawing. With contributions by: Andrea Vairelles, Anna Marino, Beth Sorby, Emilia Schönwiese, Flora Schmid, Hannah Horn, Henriette Sonntag, Leo Hasslinger, Maria Lutkova, Max Offergeld, Nikolaus Kohout, Sophie Schweizer, Anija S Dartizio, Timo Pfeifer, Vera Kügel AIL in cooperation with the department Drawing and Printmaking and Simon Goritschnig Image: Henriette Sonntag Design: Atelier Dreibholz Concept Postcard Editions and Production: Eva Weber

candidateAudit.title: For Angewandte Festival, we planned five more exhibition activations: 4 Jul 2026, 15:00 The Geography of Yellow Walls Performance by Mehrta Shirzadian mehrrta Bright yellow becomes
candidateAudit.text: For Angewandte Festival, we planned five more exhibition activations: 4 Jul 2026, 15:00 The Geography of Yellow Walls Performance by Mehrta Shirzadian mehrrta Bright yellow becomes a quiet declaration of care, resistance, and return. Here, the body is reclaimed as homeland, shaped by experience rather than imposed borders. A performance unfolding through turmeric as healing material and the body as living territory. The work is rooted in a deep commitment to women’s health and critical scientific perspectives, engaging forms of embodied knowledge that have long been ignored or erased. The body becomes both evidence and memory, offering its own geography as a space of protection, defiance, and belonging. The performance is adapted to each site, responding to the spatial and contextual conditions of different venues. Mehrta Shirzadian is a performance and multimedia artist and artistic ­researcher working at the intersection of art and science. With a background in molecular biology, mathematics, and computer science, she creates participatory works exploring microbial life, sound, and bodily ecologies, addressing embodiment, agency, and the politics of representation. Part of the exhibition [REVERBERATED]. candidateAudit.text: On view till Saturday (18:00) – An installation presented by the department of Digital Arts / Part of Angewandte Festival René’s Collapse Collection’ is a fictional startup and alternative investment platform that explores the cultural, economic, and emotional afterlife of the collapse of René Benko’s SIGNA empire. Through NFTs, merchandise, video works, and performative sales strategies, the project examines how value is produced through speculation, narrative, and collective belief. Originally developed through public interventions, the project was expanded through a student take over by Digitale Kunst. This exhibition presents new project strands developed by the students: an NFT series reflecting on financial dependency, a merchandise collection appropriating the aesthetics of startup culture and luxury branding, and a series of short-form videos combining influencer culture, promotional performance, and social commentary. Operating at the intersection of installation, performance, and participatory fiction, Renés Collapse Collection invites visitors to engage directly with the mechanisms of speculation, value production, and collapse. A project by by Zora Hünermann and Jakob Margit With contributions by: Ulrike Fritzsche, Koschka Cosmo Keye, Juarez Suarez, Ghanishka Kedar, Sei Jeung, Ghazal Naeimi, Dongjoo Kim, Jazzmin, Margherita Pruneti, Nicolás Henao Bonnet, Roma Bogdanov, and Grisha Terno.

candidateAudit.text: In a world that is seemingly always connected, we lose ourselves in constant contact. As part of Angewandte Festival, AIL presents: Sich zusammen schreiben [to get in touch], A performance and poem by Carla Schwering and Timna Lugstein from by the department of Institute of Fine Arts & Media Art – Photography (Sophie Thun) The phrase "Schreiben wir uns zusammen" that on the surface means something like “let’s write to each other again in more detail” actually implies a postponement. In the performance, the artists type excerpts from their shared chat history in a poetic arrangement on two typewriters facing each other – messages in which they attempt to get closer to one another. The time and effort spent cancelling meet ups, for which there is supposedly no capacity is made visible. With the postcards created for the performance, visitors can reconnect with a long-lost friend. On the occasion of Angewandte Festival AIL hosts a selection of performances and installations in the cashier hall and the current exhibition will have more activations. candidateAudit.text: For Angewandte Festival, we planned five more exhibition activations: 3 Jul 2026, 15:30 Darf ich noch einen Satz? (Palimpsest for 8 speakers) Performance by Leonard Otterbein leonard.ottb The audio performance Darf ich noch einen Satz? (Palimpsest for 8 speakers) explores how sound can model processes of memory formation and transformation. Layered oscillations and brief sound textures repeat with phase shifts, gradually overlapping and partially canceling each other out, much like the traces in an overwritten manuscript. The work is inspired by memory research on reconsolidation – in which recalling an event alters its stored form – and its cultural studies counterpart, reconstructivity. The piece is composed of multiple layers of sound that continuously overlap anew, attempting to cancel each other out in the process. In this process, however, the layers are never completely erased, so that fragments of the preceding states always remain Leonard Otterbein is a sound artist and composer with a background in ecology and ecotoxicology, where he studied mixture effects of agricultural pesticides and nanoparticles. His work spans instrumental and electroacoustic composition, examining perceptual thresholds. He works with psychoacoustic effects and approaches sound as spatial and sculptural material shaped by its relation to space. Part of the exhibition [REVERBERATED]. candidateAudit.text: From the project SENSING LIVING SYSTEMS. Exploring the Potentials of Multisensory Scenography for Systems Awareness – a performance by mueller_divjak in front of Otto Wagner Postsparkasse as part of Angewandte Festival! 'LIMINAL TRACES. Celebrating Acoustic Ecologies' is a dynamic sound lecture that understands the acoustic world as a phenomenon of resonance, shaped by connectedness and interaction. Through the live-curated interplay of field recordings, physical and digital artefacts, the performance traces sonic imprints deeply embedded in our collective memory, presenting them as a new listening experience. Developed within SENSING LIVING SYSTEMS at the AIL, this solar performance explores the intersections of sound, pop history and solar energy, celebrating concept, improvisation and the (unexpected) emergent. The performance ends when the energy collected by the mobile solar unit runs out. — The artist and researcher duo MUELLER-DIVJAK (Dr. Jeanette Müller and Dr. Paul Divjak), who conceived and initiated SENSING LIVING SYSTEMS, is working since 2023 at AIL with international artists and systems scientists to form experiential spaces by artistic means (scenographies) and to create sensory impressions that help us to better understand and resonate with living systems. During the project essential principles of living systems are transformed into olfactory, auditory and tactile artworks / artefacts and used experimentally. Team: Jeanette Müller, Paul Divjak, Alexandra Graupner, Anna-Maria Irgang

candidateAudit.text: For Angewandte Festival, we planned five more exhibition activations: 3 July 2026, 15:00 Hypervigilant Performance by Leah Barbara Mukui Giertz iukumukui Part of the exhibition [REVERBERATED]. Following the Movement of Memory artscience.ak Constant vigilance can develop as a response to racial discrimination and transgenerational trauma, allowing potential threats to be recognized in advance. This fight-or-flight state activates the nervous system and can lead to chronic muscle tension and bruxism. Teeth grinding occurs as a way of coping with stress during sleep, often driven by societal expectations to suppress fear or anger. Hypervigilant addresses this suppressed anger. Aluminum teeth suspended from the ceiling form a space similar to a cage that oscillates between protection and exposure. Shaped as gong-like instruments, the oversized representation of the artist’s bite is set into vibration during a sound performance to release embodied pressure and reduce tension in the nervous system. Leah Barbara Mukui Giertz’s practice centers on suppressed experiences expressed in imagined worlds. Through performative sculptures and installations, she examines spatial dynamics and power structures. Addressing socio-political themes such as racism, sexism, gender, and sexuality, she builds subconscious environments using reference-based objects and constructions in combination with text and sound. candidateAudit.text: As part of Angewandte Festival, AIL presents: Performance by Laura Oyuela and Ádám Salomvári (students of the department Cross-Disciplinary Strategies) Rocks, I mean; - Stars is a sonic and spatial performance departing from text, soundscapes, spoken words and its physical surrounding. The piece works with analogies between black holes and human beings through low frequencies, orbital motion, and stretched time, shaping a field that gathers bodies into one another. The project investigates how perceptual, cognitive, and affective dynamics shape the experience of artistic performance in relation to contemporary conditions of subjectivity, particularly isolation and hyperproductivity. The performance is part of the Cross-Disciplinary Strategies Master’s program exhibition 2026. The work is realised with the technical support of ÆSR Lab, which has contributed to its sonic and spatial development. Photo: earthboundeva

Following the Movement of Memory with master students from artscience.ak (free entry, no registrations needed): 25 June, 15:00 2 July, 17:00 3 July, 17:00 4 July, 17:00 9 July, 17:00 Memory is not a stable record of the past. Rather than functioning as a static archive, it unfolds as a dynamic process in which traces are continuously reshaped by perception, narration, and material conditions. [REVERBERATED] explores notions of memory as the annual exhibition of the master’s program Art & Science. The exhibition approaches this process through the metaphor of reverberation. Reverberation describes the reflection of sound from multiple surfaces, producing many overlapping echoes at once. Just as sound continues to resonate within a space, memories reverberate through bodies, media, and environments long after the events that created them.
